chapter: Early Los Angeles and first bands
title: C.P. Johnson's band at the Wave Cafe on the Long Beach pier
summary: He played at the Wave Cafe with C.P. Johnson, Jack McVea and Alton Redd, earning a share of a sailors' kitty larger than the salary.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: All right. The band that I think that I remember most, and I guess it's the only band I really do remember playing with at that time, I think it was the C.P. Johnson band; they were working at the beach, and the name of the band was C.P. Johnson.

And in that band was -- Jack MacVez was in that band; I just can't remember, you know, all the musicians in the band, it was like 5 or 6 pieces, and Alton Redd was in the band, and I used to take his place and play, but that was -- I know, the name of the place on the pier in Long Beach was called the Wave Cafe, and the guys used to work; they got, I think it was $3.50 per night, and they got the kitty.
And the sailors would come in and they would request songs and they would put money in the kitty.
How big did the kitty get?

Oh yeah, the kitty would get bigger than the salary was, you know, because as I told you, I would work free for the guys but when we would get off, they had to split the kitty with me, so I would go home with $5 or $6
or $5.75 or $6.75, you know, but the kitty was always much larger than the salary, which they were working for.
Now, after that experience with them, I'm gonna try and be specific about the years which is always, as I told you, it's hard for me to do.
